title: Winter Sports and Snow

parts.title: Notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: SKI HIRE: Skis, boots and sticks can be hired by the day or by the week. Prices are cheaper if you book online before you arrive.
AVALANCHE WARNING: Today the risk on the north slopes is high. Please stay on the marked paths and follow the instructions of the ski patrol.
SKI SCHOOL: Beginners' lessons start at 9.30 each morning. Meet your instructor at the bottom of the blue slope. Children must wear a helmet.
CAFÉ SNOWFLAKE: Hot chocolate, soup and fresh bread all day. Booking a table is not necessary, but groups of more than eight should call ahead.
LIFT PASS: Your pass works on all the lifts for the whole of your stay. Keep it in a pocket, because you must show it at every lift.

parts.title: My first time on skis
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
I had always wanted to ski, so when my uncle invited me to the mountains last February, I accepted at once. I imagined myself flying down the slope like a champion. The reality was very different.

On the first morning, my instructor, a patient woman called Heidi, took me to the beginners' slope. It was so small that even the little children laughed at me. I spent the first hour learning how to stand up, because every time I tried, I fell over again. My skis seemed to have a mind of their own.

By the afternoon, I was finally able to slide slowly down the slope without falling. I was so excited that I decided to try the next slope, which was much steeper. This was a mistake. Halfway down, I lost control, flew past a group of surprised skiers and ended up in a large pile of snow.

That evening, my legs hurt, and I could hardly walk, but I could not stop smiling. By the end of the week, I could ski down the blue slope without falling. My uncle says that I am a natural. I think he is just being kind, but I have already booked another trip for next year.

questions.prompt: What did the writer expect before the trip?
options: To feel afraid of all the snow
To spend most of the days resting
questions.explanation: He imagined himself flying down the slope like a champion.

questions.prompt: Why did children laugh at the writer?
options: He fell over on a very small slope
He could not find his own skis
questions.explanation: He kept falling on the beginners' slope.

questions.prompt: What happened on the steeper slope?
options: He skied past all of the others
He lost control and fell into snow
He met his uncle halfway down it
questions.explanation: He lost control and ended up in a pile of snow.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel that evening?
options: Too tired to talk to anyone
Angry about the fall he had
questions.explanation: His legs hurt, but he could not stop smiling.

questions.prompt: What does the writer say about his uncle's comment?
options: He is angry with his uncle
He agrees that he is a natural
He thinks his uncle is being kind
questions.explanation: He thinks his uncle is just being kind.

parts.title: Winter in the mountains
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Every winter, thousands of tourists visit the village of Alpenau, high in the mountains. [1] For six months of the year, the snow is so deep that cars cannot reach the top road, and visitors take a small red train instead.

The village is famous for its ski slopes, but there are many other things to do. [2] Many visitors enjoy a sleigh ride through the forest, pulled by two strong horses wearing warm blankets.

In the evening, the restaurants fill with hungry skiers. [3] A traditional dish is melted cheese with bread, which is cooked at the table over a small flame.

The local people are very friendly. [4] Many of them have lived in the village all their lives and are happy to tell visitors stories about the old days. [5] It is no surprise that so many people return year after year.
sentences: The first snow usually falls at the end of October.
They offer food that is simple, hot and filling.
The village has a small museum and a swimming pool.
Shopkeepers, waiters and ski teachers all enjoy a chat.
The nearest airport is about two hours away by car.
It is a magical place, especially at Christmas.

gaps.explanation: The first snow in October leads to the snow being deep for six months.
The museum and pool are other activities, followed by a sleigh ride.
The restaurants offer simple hot food, and then a traditional dish is described.
Chatting shows the friendliness, and then people telling stories.
A magical place at Christmas explains why people return every year.

My brother is much better [4] me and keeps laughing when I fall over. In the evening, we sit by the fire and [5] hot chocolate. I wish you [6] here with us! See you soon, Claire

parts.title: Snow safety
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Playing in the snow is great fun, but it is also important to take care. Always wear warm clothes, including a hat and gloves, [1] you will get cold very quickly. Take a flask of hot tea or soup with you, and stop for a rest [2] you feel tired. Never go out alone, and tell somebody where you are going [3] you leave. If the weather becomes bad, return to the village [4] soon as you can. It is wise to use sun cream and sunglasses too, because the sun can be very strong on the snow. Many people forget [5] it, and they burn their faces. Remember these simple rules, [6] you will enjoy a safe holiday.

gaps.explanation: "Or" shows what will happen if you do not wear warm clothes.
Stop to rest "when" you feel tired.
"And" you will enjoy a safe holiday.

parts.title: A talk about the ski centre
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: karl
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to the Silver Mountain Ski Centre. My name is Karl. We have eighteen slopes, and the longest is six kilometres. The lifts open at half past eight and close at four, because it gets dark early. A day pass costs forty pounds, and children under eight ski for free. If you need equipment, the hire shop is next to the car park. Lessons for beginners are in the mornings, and you should book them at the information desk. For lunch, there are two cafés. The one at the top of the main lift has the best view, but it is more expensive. In the evenings, you can go skating on the ice rink, which is open until ten. Please remember to put on sun cream, even on cloudy days.

gaps.explanation: A day pass costs forty pounds.

gaps.prompt: The hire shop is next to the ___
gaps.explanation: The hire shop is next to the car park.

gaps.prompt: The ice rink is open until ___
gaps.explanation: The rink is open until ten.

parts.title: A snowboarder
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: Today's guest is Ingrid Brandt, a professional snowboarder. Ingrid, how did you start?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: My family lived near the mountains, and when I was six, I borrowed my brother's board. I fell over all day, but I loved it.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: How often do you train?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: Six days a week. In summer, I train in the gym and practise on a dry slope, because there's no snow.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: Have you ever hurt yourself?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: Yes, I broke my wrist two years ago. It took four months to heal, and I thought I'd never get back to my best.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What do you like about the sport?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: The freedom. When you are on a mountain with fresh snow and nobody around, it's an incredible feeling.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What is the hardest part?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: Being away from home for months. I miss my friends, and I eat a lot of pasta in hotel rooms.

turns.speaker: victor
turns.text: What are your plans for next season?

turns.speaker: ingrid
turns.text: I want to win a medal at the world games. I'm working hard, and I hope that it happens.
